entry.title: Pose page has been reworked
entry.summary:
The page you are looking at is reworked to have weekly grouping, although I strictly want to post small bits everyday like Mastodon posts. The only friction I feel with Mastodon is that like any other social media it still has that "Feedback Craving": when I post, I keep expecting someone to star it and reply. The constant tension of someone overlooking it might demotivate me from writing anything more. Thus here I'm writing on my own site without caring for anything, but whatever it is, this holds as a document for myself to see over the "world wide web". No reaction craving, nor any self-pitfalls.
I should write about my hate towards the reaction system altogether as a blog post, and I should find a way to hide them everywhere. I know it's very useful, but I totally hate it. At least a respectful way to hide them, as a user preference, would help. YouTube did it, but on their end; I'd prefer it on the user (client) end.

entry.title: Why have I used "Log Pose"
entry.summary:
I used "Log Pose" to depict the one piece themed site, and I went with naming all my blog posts as "Log(s)" and I made a "Pose" for a shot bits of micro notes, journal, thoughts etc etc for capturing quickly. At the time of creating my only answer was that "Log" would be long writing in-depth and "Pose" would be just some info posted ideally every day without any filter.
But I was so late to realize that "Log Pose" almost mimics the sound of "Blog post", the words are so close. I kept laughing when I re-discovered myself for this easter egg I planted myself into.

entry.title: I love animated movie and content creations
entry.summary:
It is the only place where people enjoy all imperfections. Every animated movie (west) or Anime (asia) is mostly made for comedy and fun. But its suprising how people enjoy it very much and dont get into character shaming
Whereas contrast this in real life, people feel they have imperfect body and thanks to reels and spoiled by big media, we got impression that humans as in "we" must look this way for perfection or just to be seen good. Of course hitting gym is good and staying fit should be goal of all.

entry.title: How I like/use and also hate AI
entry.summary: I talk AI in the sense of Agent or assistant as tool only here.
entry.content:
• AI is a great research companion
  • AI is a great tool to assist when brain is not working
  • AI can take the boring task and let us architect the task
  • AI is like any other crafting tool, you take the crafting art responsibility
  • A good prompt == best outcome, no blame to AI & its appreciated as a tool.
  • Only AI hatred I can feel genuinely is, if prompter does not know where the code got copied from, or from which learning it got results. Adding attributions actually help for more trust.
  • I hate people hating AI, just because of "why not". There are too many idiots who just proclaim that just because developer is using it they dismiss and fire it away. These people don't have work or things to get done TBH
  • I hate AI when it does anything more than I ask for, and goes beyong spitting out chunks of trash.
  • I hate people being divided over AI, middle ground is the only way. Both extremes are fools.
  • I hate when people think every AI user is a bad or ill-intentioned developer, these people go to extreme of not using it and even gaslighting anyone who mentions it (see mastodon threads for any)

I talk AI in the sense of Agent or assistant as tool only here.

entry.title: The comfort of borrowed choices.
entry.summary:
We have become so accustomed to what is served to us that we rarely pause to question what we actually need. From thoughts to food, entertainment to everyday choices, convenience has slowly replaced curiosity, and consumption has taken the place of creation. We mistake having endless options for having freedom, while rarely questioning who made those choices available to us in the first place.
Further reading
entry.content:

  • The Society of the Spectacle by Guy Debord
  • Amusing Ourselves to Death by Neil Postman
  • Manufacturing Consent by Edward S. Herman and Noam Chomsky
  • The Shallows by Nicholas Carr

entry.title: Amazing lessons from every moment.
entry.summary: Recently came across 30 things at 30, which led me to 50 things I know. Both are lovely reminders of how much life teaches us along the way. Not every lesson arrives at a particular age or moment; some take years to realize, while others simply need someone else's words to help us see what was already there. Life is less about learning things on time and more about recognizing them when we do.

entry.title: An echo chamber need not be silent.
entry.summary: A room full of ideas does not always make for a meaningful exchange. Sometimes everyone arrives to contribute, but few arrive to reconsider; opinions pile upon opinions, while the more practical questions remain untouched. Not everything that sounds interesting is worth pursuing, nor does every conversation necessarily move us forward.

entry.title: Haste makes servants of us all.
entry.summary: We rush to solve problems others barely care about, giving our time before they even value it. We mistake being helpful for being needed, and our haste for their urgency, only to learn that not every burden we carry is worth the weight. For time is the one price we all pay equally, regardless of what we own or what we can afford.
